 Jax Taylor reveals cancer diagnosis as he undergoes surgery: ‘In a really dark place’ 
 By 
 Riley Cardoza 
 Published 
 Nov. 19, 2026, 6:38 a.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Jax Taylor has been diagnosed with cancer.
 The “Vanderpump Rules” alum went public with his concerning health update in an Instagram post on Thursday, while opening up to his followers about the “really dark place” he’s in.
 “This is something I’ve kept private for the past few months because it’s been one of the scariest times of my life,” the former reality star, 47, wrote.
 10 
 Jax Taylor announced via Instagram on Thursday that he underwent surgery to remove a kidney tumor after a cancer diagnosis. The reality star is pictured in hospital in an image he shared with his health update. mrjaxtaylor/Instagram 
 10 
 The former reality star, pictured in a Season 2 promo photo for “The Valley” in May 2025, admitted that he is in a “really dark place.” Trae Patton/Bravo via Getty Images

 Taylor’s struggles began when he went to the hospital for what he thought was kidney stones in July — before the experience “turned into something [he] never imagined.”
 The “Valley” alum explained, “My CT scan also showed a tumor on my left kidney. After many tests and appointments, I found out it was cancer.
 “After a long five-hour surgery today, the tumor has been removed but it was a lot larger than they thought so we are waiting on the pathology results,” he continued.

 While the reality star did not share what results his doctors are waiting for, traditionally, pathology tests help to reveal the type of cancer a person is suffering from, as well as the grade of tumor, and whether it has been fully removed. 
 Taylor went on to write that he will never again take his “health for granted.”
 The Bravolebrity added, “It’s crazy how things happen. If I hadn’t ended up in the hospital with that kidney stone, I probably wouldn’t have known this tumor was there until it was too late. … Life can really change in a second.”
 10 
 Taylor is “waiting on pathology results” after his five-hour surgery to remove the growth. mrjaxtaylor/Instagram 
 10 
 He will never again take his “health for granted.” mrjaxtaylor/Instagram 
 Elsewhere in his lengthy caption, Taylor noted that his dad, Ronald Cauchi, died of esophageal and throat cancer in December 2017 at age 61.
 Taylor also praised his “amazing girlfriend,” Lori Krebs , for being his “rock.”
 The former Sur bartender, who included a shot of Krebs in his carousel of hospital photos, gushed, “She’s been my rock through all of this. She’s not just my partner, she’s my best friend and I feel so insanely lucky to have her in my life.”
 10 
 “It’s crazy how things happen,” Taylor, pictured in February 2025 in Los Angeles, wrote. GC Images 
 10 
 He went on to give a shoutout to girlfriend Lori Krebs for being his “rock.” mrjaxtaylor/Instagram 
 Taylor previously believed he had cancer during a Season 2 episode of “Vanderpump Rules,” with him showing Tom Sandoval and Tom Schwartz growths on his pectoral muscles.
 “I got X-rays. They’re gonna run some tests,” he said at the time — but was ultimately given a clean bill of health.
 Taylor’s current cancer battle comes as he is navigating his contentious divorce and custody battle from ex Brittany Cartwright.
 10 
 He is currently navigating his divorce from Cartwright, whom he split from in 2024. mrjaxtaylor/Instagram 
 10 
 The former “Vanderpump Rules” stars are the parents of 5-year-old son Cruz. Instagram/@littlebabycauchi 
 The former couple, who split in 2024 after nearly five years of marriage , are the parents of 5-year-old son Cruz .
 Most recently, Taylor demanded Cartwright, 37, pay him $17,000 per month in spousal support , claiming she has “sabotaged” his ability to earn a living due to an alleged “deliberate and sustained campaign” to damage his reputation.
 Cartwright, notably, was granted a temporary restraining order in August after accusing her former spouse of “coercive control, financial abuse, emotional and psychological abuse, gaslighting and even physical violence .”
